ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Prior to incorporation, the proposed Korean legal counsel must conduct enhanced due diligence on all initial members, directors, the ultimate beneficial owner or owners, and all authorized signatories against the U.S. OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list, the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, the UK Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation list, and the Republic of Korea financial sanctions list maintained by the Financial Services Commission. The protocol must automatically detect politically exposed persons, foreign tax residency indicators, adverse media, and prior regulatory enforcement actions. Each beneficial owner at or above the 25% threshold must be positively identified through a government-issued passport, corporate registration excerpts, and the complete ownership chain. The screening must be rerun immediately before bank account opening and again upon any change in ownership, and a negative-match affidavit and video KYC interview must be retained for five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS) / Court Registry Name Search Portal maintained by the National Court Administration
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official registered corporate name must be expressed in Hangul and must follow the four-tier naming convention: (i) a distinctive principal trade name; (ii) an optional business-objective descriptor; (iii) a Hangul phonetic transliteration of any foreign original trade name, with the original Roman alphabet name shown only as an auxiliary external name; and (iv) the statutory legal entity suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa' indicating a limited liability company under the Korean Commercial Act. The proposed Hangul name must not be identical or materially indistinguishable from an existing trade name in the same or similar business or in the same court registration district, and any identity conflict must be resolved by adopting an entirely distinct transliteration or principal name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry rejects or conditions the proposed name, the applicant must obtain the written rejection grounds, prepare a revised Hangul name that eliminates the conflict or sensitive token, and file a corrective application through the same IROS portal. If the rejection is an administrative or judicial registry decision, the applicant may within fourteen days submit a formal written appeal to the competent district court under the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act, attaching the original rejection notice, a revised name search report, and the incorporation documents. The registry may grant one extension of up to twenty days upon objective cause, and the appellate court's decision is conclusive.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a cosplay costume and prop apparel manufacturer selling through Shopify and Stripe, a virtual office or commercial mailbox is not acceptable as a statutory registered place of business for corporate registration, VAT business registration, corporate bank account opening, or foreign exchange reporting. Korean tax and banking authorities require a physical place where records, inventory, employee presence, and management can be inspected. A contract serviced office with a dedicated room, a nameplate, full-time administrator presence, meeting-room inspection capacity, and a lease agreement can satisfy the test, but a pure virtual address is rejected by the National Tax Service and major licensed banks.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for field inspection: (1) registered address on the Business Registration Certificate; (2) lease or ownership proof; (3) utility bill and office signage; (4) payroll records and employee presence; (5) warehouse or inventory storage; (6) e-commerce books and tax invoices; (7) in-house accounting or outsourced bookkeeping records. Quantified risk: low-to-moderate, approximately 30-40% during the first year if a genuine serviced office is maintained; high, approximately 60-75% within 24 months if a bare virtual mailbox or residential address is used, especially for apparel and costume merchants with recurring Stripe and Shopify sales.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic tax portal: Home Tax Service (HomeTax) at www.hometax.go.kr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a domestic Korean LLC, the registration is completed at the district tax office after incorporation, receiving a Business Registration Number (BRN), which serves as the TIN and VAT ID. For a foreign non-resident entity, the process is: (1) assess whether the entity has a fixed place of business (domestic place of business) or makes taxable digital supplies to Korean consumers; (2) appoint a Korean tax representative if no domestic place of business exists; (3) prepare certified copies of the foreign registration certificate, articles of incorporation and relevant resolutions, a notarized power of attorney addressed to the tax representative, and documents proving the business premise (lease agreement or equivalent); (4) file the prescribed business registration application form (Business Registration Application) with the competent district tax office in person or via the HomeTax portal; (5) the NTS verifies the documents and issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number; (6) the tax representative then becomes the joint addressee for all tax notices and must submit an e-tax invoice issuance bond or guarantee if required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box classification election is available under the Korean Corporate Tax Act; a Korean LLC is automatically treated as a resident corporation subject to entity-level corporate income tax. None of the OECD hybrid mismatch or US-style pass-through elections apply. A domestic group may elect consolidated corporate tax filing under the Corporate Tax Act if all conditions for a wholly-owned group are met.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax) under the Value Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary threshold for regular VAT registration; every person supplying taxable goods or services in the course of business must register. Simplified taxpayer threshold: annual taxable turnover below KRW 80,000,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT tax invoices must be issued electronically through the HomeTax e-tax invoice system and transmitted to the NTS within the statutory period. No real-time fiscal clearance or anti-fraud digital stamping is used; instead, the NTS operates a centralized e-invoice clearing database and requires cash receipts to be issued in registered consumer retail transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported goods qualify for 0% VAT when the goods are exported outside Korea (Korean customs territory) and the export sale is evidenced by a customs export declaration and foreign currency settlement. Any goods exported under the Manufacturing Drawback or Free Trade Zone regime also qualify. Zero-rating additionally applies to services supplied to non-residents if the services are performed overseas or are not connected with Korean real estate or moveable property, and the consideration is settled in foreign currency.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Declaration Receipt) issued by Korea Customs Service
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB)
Foreign Exchange Bank Certificate of Export Proceeds (Foreign Exchange Purchase or Receipt Certificate)
Export Sales Contract or Purchase Order (when requested by the NTS)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS conducts post-audit reviews of zero-rating claims. Failure to produce sufficient export documentation or to repatriate export proceeds within the statutory deadline reverses the zero-rating and triggers assessment of VAT at 10% plus interest. Penalties may reach 40% of the unpaid VAT for intentional or fraudulent claims and 20% for negligent under-reporting. Criminal sanctions under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act may apply for forged or falsely issued export documents.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), acting as the central bank, together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF), under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and subordinate Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a heavily liberalised yet administratively supervised foreign exchange regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The won is convertible for current account purposes, including trade-related payments and profit remittance, once the underlying documentation and reporting are completed through a registered foreign exchange bank. Capital account convertibility is conditional: inflows such as foreign direct investment, equity injections into a Korean limited liability company, and loans must be reported or approved depending on notifiable thresholds. There are no general surrender requirements for export proceeds, but a resident exporter must receive the contracted proceeds within the statutory collection period, normally one year from the export date, and any unreceived balance must be reported. Dividend and profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is permitted after corporate tax reconciliation, with remission evidenced by audited financial statements, tax clearance certificates, and foreign exchange purpose codes for overseas remittance. The Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Bank of Korea operate a negative-list supervision framework; certain transactions involving cross-border guarantees, derivatives, or foreign exchange risk exceeding thresholds still require registration through a designated foreign exchange bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Statutory collection period is one year from the date of export declaration or final loading, with a possible extension of up to six months approved by the responsible foreign exchange bank for documented force majeure or receivables prolongation. Mandatory conversion ratio: 0%. Export proceeds may be retained in a foreign currency account, provided the exporter maintains the bank-in record and submits the export credit collection report to the customs clearance system. Failure to collect within the period triggers a report to the Bank of Korea and may expose the entity to administrative penalty and adverse FX transaction history.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: 10/100. Not viable as a primary corporate banking rail. Offshore fintech EMIs such as Revolut, Airwallex, or Payoneer are not licensed in South Korea to open domestic corporate operating accounts or process Korean won settlements for this resident entity. Korean law requires resident legal entities to maintain accounts with institutions registered under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and authorized as foreign exchange banks under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. An unlicensed offshore EMI cannot be used as the main clearing rail because it may violate foreign exchange financial transactions reporting and may not support the mandatory customer identification requirements. Such EMIs can only serve as auxiliary receiving channels where settlement is ultimately routed to a Korean licensed bank account; even then, each inbound remittance must be assigned the correct FX purpose code and disclosed if the aggregate amount crosses the reporting threshold.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-branch physical presence is mandatory for incorporation accounts that require corporate identity certification. Under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act and bank KYC guidelines, at least one statutory director and the beneficial owner or majority controlling shareholder must appear before a bank officer with the original corporate seal certificate, business registration certificate, and passport. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally accepted for a domestic Korean limited liability company because the bank must verify the representative's real name and duty of care. Non-resident shareholders must also provide evidence of lawful foreign exchange remittance and source of funds before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO and shareholder chain for a non-resident controlling investor, particularly if a trust or intermediate foreign holding company is used.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry abstracts of every layer up to the natural persons, UBO declaration countersigned by each director, FATF-style ownership diagram, source of funds and source of wealth reports, audited financial statements of intermediate entities, and passport or alien registration details with proof of address.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from offshore parent without recognized foreign exchange investment registration, creating a false valuation or potential disguised overseas borrowing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign Exchange Investment Declaration filed with the designated foreign exchange bank, bank-in proof of wire remittance from the investor's own account, board resolution authorizing issuance of shares, share subscription agreement, independent certified public accountant capital verification report, and loan-related documents if any portion is debt financing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Royalty and IP license payments to overseas licensors for theatrical and cosplay character rights from a non-FATF high-risk jurisdiction, with missing withholding tax evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed trademark and copyright license or sales agency agreements, domestic IP registration certificates, royalty calculation model and transfer pricing documentation, KRW withholding remittance slips and tax payment certificates for business income, foreign exchange purpose code declarations, and OECD CRS status declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity retail aggregator settlement mismatch between Shopify and Stripe payouts and declared export invoices, producing fragmented amounts from high-chargeback consumers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant account settlement statements mapped to export declarations and Korea Customs Service export report, platform payout ledger, chargeback and refund policy documentation, consumer identity metadata, warehouse shipping manifests and delivery tracking, and treasury reconciliation report signed by an external auditor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity subscription proceeds by SWIFT MT103 from the investor's own bank account to a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank, citing the foreign exchange purpose code for equity investment in a domestic company. The receiving bank files the foreign exchange receipt and use declaration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; if the amount equals or exceeds the statistical reporting threshold, it is reported automatically to the Bank of Korea. After remittance, a certified public accountant issues the capital verification report, the bank updates the shareholder paid-in capital record, and the entity registers the contribution in the corporate registry at the applicable market exchange rate. Any side-loan or convertible instrument must be separately documented to avoid misclassification as undisclosed debt.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for routine trade invoices and royalty payments below the bank's documentary threshold. Use Commercial Letters of Credit for recurring bulk purchases of costume fabrics, wigs, and prop components from established Asian and European suppliers, with the Korean bank as issuing bank. Use Documentary Collections for lower-risk repeat counterparties where open-account settlement is acceptable. All outbound payments for licensed IP royalties, dividends, and service fees must include the correct foreign exchange remittance purpose code and evidence of tax withholding to avoid rejection by the foreign exchange surveillance system.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: KRW/USD deliverable forward contracts with licensed onshore foreign exchange banks for verified trade exposure up to the contracted export or import amount

Non-deliverable forwards on the Korean won with a licensed onshore or approved offshore bank, settled in USD, to hedge receivables denominated in won where non-resident counterparties cannot receive won
Cross-currency interest rate swaps between KRW and USD or JPY permitted when an underlying external borrowing or funding facility exists and has been reported to the Bank of Korea
Zero-cost collar options and vanilla options permitted for commercial hedge purposes, subject to submission of an FX transaction report and proof of real economic exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Tax Return (Corporate Tax, as per the Corporate Tax Act, Article 60) including annual settlement of semi-annual prepayments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) – jurisdictional district tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 next following a calendar fiscal year; if fiscal year is not calendar, within three (3) months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Underpayment penalty of 20% of reported tax if the net tax payable is overstated or understated; negligence penalty of 10% of the overstated credit amount; an additional daily delinquency interest charge of 0.023% per day (approximately 8.4% per annum) on the unpaid balance; eventual seizure of assets and initiation of criminal investigation upon persistent failure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Value-Added Tax (VAT) final returns for the first and second half-year tax periods
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) / jurisdictional tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half final return on or before July 25; second half final return on or before January 25 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: VAT submission deficiency penalty of 0.5% of the unreported or underreported taxable base; false-report penalty of 1% of the false amount; daily interest of 0.3% per month (0.01% per day) on unpaid VAT; revocation of business registration in case of repeated failure to file

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Surtax filing with the local government (municipal / county revenue division)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government (Si / Gun / Gu) tax collection department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the NTS corporate tax return; by March 31 for calendar-year taxpayers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A surcharge of 10% to 20% of the local income tax amount due; interest on arrears of 3% per year above the statutory interest rate; seizure of local tax receivables and prohibition on tax clearance certificates for overdue taxpayers

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary general meeting of the Yuhan Hoesa and statutory registration of any changes concerning directors, members, and registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate governance (no government filing unless a registrable change exists; the change registration is filed with the Commercial Registration Board of the district court)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ordinary meeting no later than March 31 (within three months after fiscal year-end); registrable change must be filed within four (4) weeks of the change under the Commercial Registration Act as applied in Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the ordinary meeting results in fine-for-noncompliance; late registration of a commercial change is sanctioned by the commercial registration court with a penalty surcharge of KRW 50,000 (approx. USD 38) and an administrative order; persistent failure may suspend the entity's right to use the corporate name and expose the Yuhan Hoesa to involuntary dissolution

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Companies, an independent certified public accountant audit is mandatory if the entity's (a) total assets amount to KRW 12 billion (approx. USD 9.0 million) or more at the end of the fiscal year; (b) total liabilities amount to KRW 7 billion (approx. USD 5.2 million) or more and total revenue to KRW 20 billion (approx. USD 15 million) or more; or (c) the entity is a 'public-interest company' designated by the Financial Services Commission (e.g., listed on a Korean securities market). There is no direct statutory headcount threshold; however an audit will apply if the company qualifies through the asset-revenue test and is not an exempt small enterprise.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) are mandatory for public-interest companies. A private Yuhan Hoesa below the audit threshold may elect to apply the General Purpose Financial Statements standard for Small and Medium Enterprises (K-GAAP), or K-IFRS, but must present fair presentation in either framework; all statements must be denominated in KRW and comply with the Korean Accounting Standards Board's guidance.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under current Korean law, no separate UBO annual declaration is required for a non-financial, low-risk Yuhan Hoesa unless the company engages in a specific financial-type business (e.g., virtual assets, AML-designated sectors). Nevertheless, the member registry must be updated on a current basis, and any transfer of membership shall be reported on the statutory register within thirty (30) days, effectively serving as an annual true-up confirmation at the ordinary general meeting; the members and directors must approve and sign the annual financial statements, thereby perpetually confirming the ownership and management structure.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 – 900 per annum for a licensed corporate secretary and registered-address service in Seoul
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 – 7,500 for an independent CPA audit if the entity crosses the statutory audit threshold; USD 0 if the entity remains below the KRW 12 billion asset test and is exempt

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: For tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2025: 10% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 20% on the portion from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 22% on the portion from KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion; and 25% on the portion exceeding KRW 300 billion. A separately imposed local corporate income tax generally adds 10% of the national corporate income tax, producing combined marginal rates of 11%, 22%, 24.2%, and 27.5%, respectively. Apply the rates and transitional rules in force for the relevant tax year.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday applies solely because the entity is a Yuhan Hoesa or manufactures cosplay apparel. A qualifying small or medium-sized enterprise may claim statutory special tax reductions for qualifying business income, subject to current law, regional conditions, ownership and size tests, and exclusions. Qualifying investments may receive investment tax credits, subject to asset, business, timing, and recapture rules. Incentives require contemporaneous evidence and may be restricted for related-party or nonqualifying activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: National Corporate Tax Return (Corporate Tax Base and Tax Amount Report, 법인세 과세표준 및 세액신고서) and required schedules filed electronically through the National Tax Service Hometax system. The Korean legal form name is provided only as an official form identifier.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return; interim corporate tax prepayment is generally required for a qualifying corporation.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File and pay within three months after the end of the fiscal year. A corporation with a December 31 year-end generally files by March 31. Interim prepayment is generally due within two months after the first six months of the fiscal year, subject to statutory exemptions and calculation alternatives. Check the applicable year's extension and holiday rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the corporation's business registration number, legal name, registered address, representative, tax office, and fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-owned Korean corporation reports its Korean entity details and Korean tax registration, not the foreign shareholder's details as the taxpayer. Disclose foreign ownership and related-party information in the applicable schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile financial accounting profit or loss to taxable income by identifying non-deductible expenses, deductible adjustments, timing differences, and other statutory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include income attributable to the Korean corporation's business and apply Korean tax rules. Do not omit related-party charges, foreign-source items, or permanent establishment issues merely because a counterparty is non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the tax base after permitted deductions and losses, with year-of-origin and utilization details for carried-forward losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use only losses legally available to the Korean taxpayer and observe applicable ownership-change, business-continuity, limitation, and documentation rules. The general carryforward period is up to 15 years, subject to statutory restrictions and the relevant loss vintage.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the progressive corporate tax brackets applicable to the tax year, then calculate credits, reductions, minimum tax where applicable, and final national tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the Korean resident corporation rules to a Korean-incorporated Yuhan Hoesa. A foreign shareholder's residence does not convert the Korean corporation into a non-resident taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate and report local corporate income tax under the Local Tax Act using the relevant tax base and rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File and pay the local tax through the designated local tax system or linked electronic process. Confirm local tax deadlines and any filing data carried over from the national return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax credits, reductions, and supporting schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim only available statutory incentives and attach prescribed schedules, investment records, eligibility calculations, and supporting documents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign ownership alone does not establish incentive eligibility. Preserve evidence of qualifying activity, assets, employment, location, and compliance with incentive conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Complete prescribed disclosures for cross-border related-party transactions, transfer pricing, overseas subsidiaries, and other international tax matters.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the ultimate parent and related parties accurately. Reconcile disclosures to transfer pricing documentation, customs records, withholding returns, and intercompany agreements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Submit the return electronically and pay the assessed balance by the statutory deadline. Retain the electronic receipt and supporting records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign owners should ensure the Korean corporation maintains a local authorized tax representative or responsible officer for filing, payment, and audit communications.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing may trigger a return-filing penalty generally based on a percentage of unpaid tax, with higher treatment for fraudulent conduct and possible reductions for qualifying voluntary late filing. Underreporting penalties are generally 10% for ordinary underreporting and may rise to 40% for fraudulent or materially deceptive conduct. Late payment additional tax generally accrues at 0.022% per day on unpaid amounts, subject to current statutory rules. Separate penalties may apply for inaccurate international transaction disclosures, failure to submit required transfer pricing reports, deficient invoices, and failure to withhold or remit tax. Penalties and interest are assessed under the law effective for the relevant period.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Interim Corporate Tax Prepayment Return, filed through National Tax Service Hometax where required.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Generally semiannual prepayment for a qualifying corporation; statutory exceptions may apply.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally within two months after the end of the first six months of the fiscal year. The amount is determined under the statutory prior-year or interim-period method, as applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify the corporation, fiscal year, and six-month interim period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Korean corporation's tax registration and fiscal year; foreign shareholders do not file this return in place of the corporation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Interim taxable income or prior-year basis
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the applicable interim-period tax computation or statutory prior-year prepayment basis and relevant adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Korean tax accounting and retain the computations supporting the selected statutory method.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the required prepayment after applicable credits and prior payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the prepayment to the annual tax provision and actual cash payments; do not treat a foreign tax payment as a Korean prepayment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or insufficient prepayment can result in additional tax or collection measures under the Corporate Tax Act. Unpaid amounts may accrue late-payment additional tax, generally at 0.022% per day, subject to current rules.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: For dividends paid by a Korean corporation to a non-resident beneficial owner, the domestic withholding rate is generally 20% national tax plus 2% local income tax, for a combined 22%, before treaty relief. A tax treaty may reduce the rate, commonly subject to ownership, beneficial ownership, residence, limitation-on-benefits, and anti-abuse conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid tax residence certificate from the recipient's competent tax authority and the prescribed Korean treaty-relief application and beneficial-owner documentation. Submit the documents to the Korean withholding agent within the applicable statutory period so the agent can apply relief at source where permitted. If relief at source is unavailable or excess tax was withheld, the foreign recipient may apply for a refund through the National Tax Service within the applicable limitation period. Confirm treaty eligibility, direct or indirect ownership thresholds, limitation-on-benefits provisions, principal-purpose tests, and required translations or authentication. A certificate of residence alone does not establish beneficial ownership or treaty entitlement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic withholding is generally 20% national tax plus 2% local income tax, for a combined 22%, on Korean-source royalties and interest paid to a non-resident, subject to statutory exceptions and characterization rules. Applicable treaties commonly reduce rates, but the precise rate depends on the treaty, payment type, recipient status, beneficial ownership, and any permanent establishment connection. Payments for software, know-how, trademarks, copyright, services, or equipment must be characterized from the contract and actual conduct; a treaty business-profits article may apply in some cases. The Korean payer generally withholds and remits tax by the statutory monthly deadline.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: For mandatory local file and master file reporting, the general thresholds are annual cross-border related-party transaction amounts of at least KRW 50 billion and annual sales of at least KRW 100 billion, subject to statutory definitions, aggregation rules, exemptions, and applicable year rules. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to a qualifying multinational group with consolidated revenue of at least KRW 1 trillion. Separate international transaction information disclosures may apply below these documentation thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not generally apply a UAE-style stand-alone Economic Substance Regulations regime. Korean tax authorities may nevertheless apply substance-over-form principles, transfer pricing rules, beneficial ownership analysis, controlled foreign corporation rules, anti-treaty-shopping provisions, and general anti-avoidance rules. Contracts, personnel, decision-making, functions, assets, risks, and actual conduct should support the reported allocation of income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and false tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing sales, fabricating costs, maintaining false books, intentionally omitting taxable income, or using sham transactions to reduce tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, ordinary or aggravated underreporting penalties, late-payment additional tax, and criminal prosecution. Aggravated tax evasion can result in imprisonment and fines under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act and, where applicable, the Act on the Aggravated Punishment of Specific Crimes. The precise penalty depends on amount, intent, duration, and statutory thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible officers may face personal criminal liability for their own participation, instruction, or knowing approval. Tax debts do not automatically pierce the corporate veil; separate statutory secondary liability, fraudulent-transfer, or criminal rules may apply. Travel restrictions may be imposed only where statutory collection or criminal procedure conditions are met.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing manipulation and deficient documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing related-party goods, services, royalties, or loans outside the arm's-length range; unsupported cost allocations; or failure to submit required international transaction reports or documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income adjustments, additional corporate tax, interest or late-payment additional tax, and penalties for failure to file or inaccurate reporting. Failure to submit required transfer pricing documentation can attract statutory penalties, including fixed or transaction-based amounts, depending on the report and applicable law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate exposure is primary. Officers may face personal administrative or criminal consequences where they knowingly falsify records, obstruct an audit, or participate in tax offenses. Maintain contemporaneous benchmarking and transaction-level support.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding tax and dividend repatriation failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, interest, or other Korean-source income to a non-resident without correct classification, withholding, remittance, or treaty eligibility review.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Korean withholding agent may be assessed the unpaid withholding tax, late-payment additional tax, and applicable penalties. Treaty relief claimed without adequate residence, beneficial ownership, or anti-abuse support may be denied and recovered.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible officers may incur personal exposure for intentional tax evasion, false certification, or other statutory offenses. The company should retain residence certificates, relief applications, contracts, payment records, and beneficial-owner analysis.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Payroll, employment, and social insurance noncompliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misclassifying employees as contractors, failing to withhold employment income tax, omitting wages or benefits, or failing to enroll and contribute as required.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Back taxes, social insurance contributions, late charges, administrative penalties, and potential criminal sanctions for deliberate evasion or falsification. Classification depends on the actual working relationship, not the contract label.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible officers may face personal liability for deliberate violations or offenses under applicable tax and employment statutes. Maintain payroll, work-status, withholding, and contribution records.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing income through an entity lacking genuine decision-making or commercial functions to obtain treaty benefits, conceal the beneficial owner, or shift profits without corresponding functions, assets, and risks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Treaty relief may be denied, income may be recharacterized, and tax, interest, and penalties may be assessed under transfer pricing and anti-avoidance rules. Sham transactions or fabricated records may also expose participants to criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal consequences for knowingly implementing sham arrangements or making false declarations. There is no automatic veil piercing solely because an entity has limited substance; liability depends on statutory grounds and individual conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-money laundering and suspicious payment activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using corporate accounts to conceal beneficial ownership or the source or destination of funds, falsifying transaction purposes, or knowingly facilitating prohibited or suspicious transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Financial institutions may file suspicious transaction reports, restrict or terminate accounts, and require enhanced due diligence. Criminal and administrative sanctions may arise under applicable anti-money laundering, proceeds-of-crime, foreign exchange, and related statutes depending on the conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and employees may be personally prosecuted where they knowingly participate in laundering, concealment, or false reporting. A travel ban or imprisonment is not an automatic tax consequence and requires an applicable statutory or judicial basis.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate records, audit obstruction, and electronic filing failures
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Destroying or withholding accounting records, submitting materially false electronic filings, failing to retain supporting documents, or obstructing a lawful tax audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties, adverse tax adjustments, recordkeeping penalties, additional tax, and potential criminal liability for intentional falsification or obstruction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible officers may be personally liable for their own unlawful acts or statutory offenses. Preserve books, invoices, customs records, intercompany agreements, tax returns, and electronic communications for the legally required retention period.
